own.T: State land (school trust and other state agencies)

acc.W: FWP wildlife management area — hunting allowed per FWP’s lands layer; refer to the current hunting regulations. Winter-range WMAs are closed to public entry from the day after the general deer/elk season (or Dec. 1, whichever is later) to noon May 15, as posted; Blackfoot Clearwater WMA keeps Cottonwood Creek and the DU pond open for ducks and geese (2026 FWP regs p. 5).
acc.F: FWP fishing access site — hunting allowed per FWP’s lands layer; weapon and no-hunting safety zones may apply. Check the site’s page (myfwp.mt.gov/fishMT/explore) before you hunt.
acc.S: Montana state park — hunting allowed per FWP’s lands layer; restrictions such as no-hunting safety zones or weapon limits may apply. Contact the park (fwp.mt.gov/stateparks).
acc.B: Block Management Area — private land enrolled by FWP for public hunting; check the BMA’s own rules, sign-in and any closed or no-shooting areas inside it. Hunting on a BMA is by FWP’s agreement with the landowner.
acc.A: FWP access-program land (public access land agreement, unlocking public land, regional access project or conservation easement) — public hunting access under a FWP agreement; check the program’s rules and the posted boundaries.
acc.G: Federal land (BLM, U.S. Forest Service, Bureau of Reclamation) — generally open to hunting, but parts are closed or restricted; ask the local federal office. Access across private land needs the owner’s permission (2026 FWP regs p. 5).
acc.T: State land — school trust land is open to hunters with a Conservation License, but check DNRC closures and restrictions: motorized travel only on public or designated roads, no firearms within 1/4 mile of inhabited buildings without permission (2026 FWP regs p. 5). Includes other state-agency land.
